label: AQ 0011
title: The skill that was never tried

questions.q: Isn't Voyager also an agent writing its own skills?
questions.a: Yes. The difference is what it writes from: code that ran and was checked. Anthropic's guide also has the model write skills, after doing the task. Who writes matters less than what they write from.

questions.q: What if your runs come from a mediocre agent?
questions.a: Then the skill records what worked, even if clumsily, which is still real. The A/B test stops anything that doesn't beat having no skill.

questions.q: What if there's no test to confirm a run?
questions.a: Use a separate checker, as Voyager did, but treat it as weaker than a test. Add a person's review, or a real outcome such as whether the change was accepted.

teach.title: How it works: building a skill from runs

questions.q: Why can't a skill written from the task description add new information?
questions.a: Everything in it comes from the description and what the model already believed. Nothing was tried against the real system, so nothing new was learned.

questions.q: Give the three reasons the SkillsBench audit found for self-written skills hurting.
questions.a: The solver often never opened them; writing them used up the run; and when used, their confident wrong steps were followed without checking.

teach.title: How it works: building a skill from runs

questions.q: What two checks should a skill pass before it ships?
questions.a: It's built from a run that a test (or a separate checker) confirmed, and it beats no skill in an A/B test on the same tasks.
